<ns0:div xmlns:ns0="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2" type="chapter">
               <ns0:head>CHAP. II.</ns0:head>
               <ns0:p>ANd when the day of Pentecost <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">This feast was fifty days after the feast of unleavened bread or Passover, as <ns0:hi>Levit.</ns0:hi> 23.16. whence it had its name, and was called the feast of weeks, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 34.22. because it was to be observed seven weeks after the feast of unleavened bread, <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 16.9. It was the feast of the first fruits of wheat Harvest, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 34.22. and on this day (to answer the Type) the spirit was poured out in such a plen<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tiful manner, as the first fruits of Christ's Ascending into Heaven; besides, the Law was given on this day, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 19.1, 11. and 'twas expedient that the Gospel (Christs Law) should be published on the same day: and it being on the first day of the week, it did recommend and honour the Lords day, as our Saviour had before by his Resurrection on that day.</ns0:note> was fully come, they were all with one accord <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">As if they had but one mind, as sent in so many bodies <ns0:hi>in one place</ns0:hi>; probably, that mentioned <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 1.13.</ns0:note> in one place.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="2">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:373" />2 And suddenly <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">The Apostles themselves not expecting it.</ns0:note> there came a sound from hea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ven, as of a rushing mighty wind <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">To pre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pare them to attend the more unto what they should hear and see afterwards: also to signifie the unexpected and pow<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />erful progress which the Gospel should have, it may be to cause the greater concourse to that place, it being an usual manner; and God would make this Miracle more publick</ns0:note>, and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 4.31.</ns0:note> it filled all the house <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">To shew that the Spirit should be bestowed on them that were met there, and on all the Church throughout the World.</ns0:note> where they were sitting.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="3">3 And there appeared unto them cloven tongues <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">To signifie the variety of Languages which the Apo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stles should be enabled to speak; to qualifie them to Preach the Gospel unto all Nations, and to remove the obstacle which the confusion of Tongues caus'd:</ns0:note>, like as of fire <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">which repre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sented, 1. The light that the Apostles should impart. 2dly. The fervent heat and zeal which they should be endued with. 3dly. The Gospel's spreading in the World, and carrying all before it, prevailing over all errors. 4thly. The purity and holiness which they and all that Preach the Gospel ought to appear withal.</ns0:note>, and it sate upon each of them <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">Remained, as far as was necessary for the founding of the <ns0:hi>Christian</ns0:hi> Religion: and was not as the gift of Prophecy<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> bestowed onely occasionally, as on <ns0:hi>Nathan, Samuel.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="4">4 And <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 1.5.</ns0:note> they were all filled with the holy Ghost <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">Those gifts and Graces which proceeded from him. The Apostles having them all in a more excellent manner than formerly, and the gift of Tongues superadded.</ns0:note>, and began <ns0:note n="‡" place="margin">Mark 16.17. Chap. 10.46. 1 Cor. 12.10, & 12, 30 & 13.1. and 14.2, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> to speak with other tongues <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">Than what were vernacular or natural to them.</ns0:note>, as the spirit gave them utterance <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, signifies more than barely to speak; implying they speak each Language in its perfection, after an Excellent, Elo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />quent and powerful manner; as from the holy Ghost whose works are perfect, <ns0:hi>non vox hominem sonat.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="5">5 And there were dwelling at Jerusalem, <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">Not onely constant Inhabitants, but such as had on occasion their Lodgings there<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> partly, out of a constant respect, which both <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> and Proselytes had for that place, (for the Temple and their worship sake; it being also a place for Learning and Education, as appears by the Col<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ledges and Synagogues mentioned, <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 6. <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.) But especially now the concourse from all parts must needs have been very great; it being one of those times in which all the Males were to appear before God. To which might be added, the great expectation they had of the Messiah, made them to omit no occasion of inquiring concerning him; the Prophecies concerning the time of his coming being fulfilled, and they could not be ignorant of the many and great things concerning the true Messiah</ns0:note> Jews, devout men, out of every nation under heaven <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">Whether the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> had been dispersed in the two or three greater, or other lesser dispersions: Thus in part was fulfilled what was Prophesied, <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 43.5.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="6">6 Now <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                     <ns0:hi>
                        <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>r.</ns0:hi> When <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> voice was <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> when this was noised <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">Either the miraculous winds was heard, or the report of what had hapned was spread abroad.</ns0:note> abroad, the multitude came together, and were <ns0:note place="margin">
                     <ns0:hi>
                        <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>r.</ns0:hi> Troubled <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> mind.</ns0:note> confounded, because that every man heard them speak in his own language <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">Probably, not that the same words spoken by the Apostles, were diversifyed according to every ones un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />derstanding: for then the miracle had been wrought in their Auditors, and not in the Apostles: but that the Apo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stles did speak to every one in their proper and most in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />telligible Language; and this was the gift of Tongues, which for some time after also was continued in the Church.</ns0:note>.<ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">Either out of shame, that they had slain <ns0:hi>Christ,</ns0:hi> whom <ns0:hi>God</ns0:hi> thus extra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ordinarily glorified; or out of admiration of so extraordinary a matter.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="7">7 And they were all amazed, and marvelled, saying one to another, Behold, are not all these which speak Galileans <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">Without Literature, or good Education, they being worse thought of on that account, than the ordinary sort of that Nation were; besides, they thought no Prophet was to be expected from <ns0:hi>Galilee, Iohn</ns0:hi> 1.46.</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="8">8 And how hear we every man in our own tongue <ns0:hi>r,</ns0:hi> wherein we were born?<ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, signifies commonly a different way of speaking, or pronouncing in the same Language; as our Southern and Northern men differ in some words and pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nunciation, tho speaking both the <ns0:hi>English</ns0:hi> Tongue. Gods works being most perfect, the Apostles might speak, not onely the same Language, which all understood, but in the same idiom and propiety of speech, which agreed to every one best.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="9">9 Parthians, and Medes, and Elamites <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">Descended from <ns0:hi>Elam, Gen.</ns0:hi> 10.22. thought to be the <ns0:hi>Persians.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>, and the dwellers in Mesopotamia <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">Between the two Rivers <ns0:hi>Tigris</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Euphrates.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>, and in Judea <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">The Apostles being <ns0:hi>Galileans,</ns0:hi> spake a distinct <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 span">
                        <ns0:desc>〈…〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> from the rest of the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> till now enabled <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 span">
                        <ns0:desc>〈…〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> did.</ns0:note>, and Cappadocia, in Pontus<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> and Asia <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">Some particular district, at <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 span">
                        <ns0:desc>〈…〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> called, as 1 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 1.1. otherwise <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 span">
                        <ns0:desc>〈…〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> in <ns0:hi>Asia</ns0:hi> in a larger sence.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="10">10 Phrygia, and <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 span">
                     <ns0:desc>〈…〉</ns0:desc>
                  </ns0:gap> and in the parts of Lybia, about <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 span">
                     <ns0:desc>〈…〉</ns0:desc>
                  </ns0:gap> and strangers <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">Who came either to <ns0:hi>Ierusalem</ns0:hi> to worship, or for any other business: It is evident, that many in or about the City of <ns0:hi>Rome,</ns0:hi> had imbraced the <ns0:hi>Iewish</ns0:hi> Religion: and of them it may be understood <ns0:hi>Iews.</ns0:hi> The other mentioned, <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 9. were such as then dwelt in <ns0:hi>Iudea,</ns0:hi> these were such as lived elsewhere, onely now came to worship or sojourn there. These were of two sorts, The one,</ns0:note> of Rome, Jews and proselytes <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">such as came over from <ns0:hi>Paganism</ns0:hi> unto the <ns0:hi>Iewish</ns0:hi> Religion, and were bound onely to observe the Precepts of <ns0:hi>Noah,</ns0:hi> and enjoy'd a liber<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ty to buy and sell, Live, and Converse amongst the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi>: hence they were called Proselytes of the gate; the ot<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>er were called Proselytes of Righteousness; for these were Circumcised, and took upon them the observation of the whole Law of <ns0:hi>Moses,</ns0:hi> and had all the priviledges belonging to the people of God.</ns0:note>,</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="11">11 Cretes <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Such as belonged to the Island of <ns0:hi>Creet,</ns0:hi> now called <ns0:hi>Candia.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>, and Arabians, we do hear them speak in our tongues the wonderful works of God <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">The wonderful works of God; those <ns0:hi>things which God had wonderfully wrought,</ns0:hi> especially the Resur<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rection of our blessed Saviour from the dead, which was a most wonderful work; and the main argument whereby the World was Converted, and unto which the Apostles bare witness.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="12">12 And they were all amazed <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">So <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 7. <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, they were as in an extasie, (the object was too strong for the faculty) they could not fa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thom the cause or reason of these wonderful things; and therefore they desire one of another to be resolved con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cerning them.</ns0:note>, and were in doubt, saying one to another, What meaneth this?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="13">13 Others <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Viz.</ns0:hi> The Scribes and Pharisees, and also the Inhabi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tants of <ns0:hi>Iury</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Ierusalem</ns0:hi>; who not understanding the Languages of other Nations, might think the Apostles did but babble, and talk idlely or rudely, when they spake with other tongues.</ns0:note> mocking said, These men are full of new wine <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">Or sweet wine; which done, may inebriate, and might be had at that time, tho the full Vintage was not yet.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="14">14 ¶ But Peter standing up <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">It speaks his extraordinary courage; after his stumbling and fall, he runs the faster, being recovered; and begins to verifie his name which our Lord had given him, shewing himself as firm and stedfast as a <ns0:hi>Rock.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> with the eleven <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">The other Apo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stles, probably, spake too in divers Languages; but by rea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />son of the shortness of St <ns0:hi>Luke's</ns0:hi> intended Narrative, and it being to the same purpose, their Sermons are omitted.</ns0:note>, lift up his voice, and said unto them, Ye men of Judea <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">Such as came from other parts of the Country;</ns0:note>, and all ye that dwell at Jerusalem <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">such as were constant Inhabitants in that City.</ns0:note>, be this known unto you, and hearken to my words:</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="15">15 For these <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">Or proves that the other Apostles spake as well as <ns0:hi>Peter,</ns0:hi> and were vindicated by him:</ns0:note> are not drunken <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">he mildly and solidly con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />futes their calumny. The</ns0:note>, as ye suppose, seeing it is but the third hour of the day <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">which answers to our nine a clock in the morning, and was the ordinary time for their morning Sacrifice and Prayer, before which time they did not eat or drink any thing; nay, 'tis thought on Festival days, it was usual with them not to eat or drink, until the sixth hour, that is, noon-time: that they might be more in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tent upon, and that fit for the service of the day. How little soever (to our shame) such an argument would be of proof now, it was in their soberer times very conclusive.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="16">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:374" />16 But this is that which was spoken by the pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phet Joel <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">God does ordinarily, before that he sends his judg<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ments, and does <ns0:hi>his strange work,</ns0:hi> endeavour to reclaim them by mercies: Not onely <ns0:hi>Ioel,</ns0:hi> but <ns0:hi>Isaiah, Ieremiah,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Ezekiel,</ns0:hi> and others Prophesied before the destruction of that people and Countrey, by <ns0:hi>Nebuchadnezzar</ns0:hi>; but now before the final and total ruine, God sent greater, and more than these, and endued them with a greater measure of the Spirit; clearer and fuller light to forewarn them of, and de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />liver them from wrath to come.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="17">17 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Isa. 44 3. Ezek. 11.19. Joel 2 28. Zech. 12 10. John 7.38.</ns0:note> And it shall <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                     <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                  </ns0:gap>ome to pass in the last days <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">In the time of the Messiah, called the <ns0:hi>last days</ns0:hi> frequent<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly, 2 <ns0:hi>Tim.</ns0:hi> 3.1. <ns0:hi>Hebr.</ns0:hi> 1.2<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> 2 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 3.3. as also called the <ns0:hi>last time,</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 1.5. 1 <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 2.18. <ns0:hi>Iude</ns0:hi> 18. because we are now under the last, and perfectest dispensation of the things of God; and no other is to be looked for until the consummation of all things.</ns0:note> saith God, <ns0:note n="‡" place="margin">Chap. 10.45.</ns0:note> I will pour out <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">Before the Spirit was given in lesser measures, and comparatively but by drops; here <ns0:hi>a little, and there a little</ns0:hi>; now more largely, even to over<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />flow.</ns0:note> of my spirit upon all flesh <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">All sorts of men, as well <ns0:hi>Gentiles</ns0:hi> as <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />trary unto their proud conceit, that God dwelt in none out of the land of <ns0:hi>Israel.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>: and your sons and your daughters <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">Fulfilled in <ns0:hi>Anna</ns0:hi> the Prophetess, <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 2.36. and in the four daughters of <ns0:hi>Philip, Chap.</ns0:hi> 21.9.</ns0:note> shall p<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                     <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                  </ns0:gap>ophesie, and your young men shall see visions <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">These were formerly, either representations more inward to their mind, as <ns0:hi>Esay's</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Ieremiah's</ns0:hi> were: or more out<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ward to their bodily eye, as <ns0:hi>Daniels</ns0:hi> was, <ns0:hi>Chap</ns0:hi> 5.5. and such as <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> had, <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 10.11.</ns0:note>, and your old men shall dream dreams <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">By dreams God some<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />times manifested his will, as to <ns0:hi>Ioseph</ns0:hi>; but this is by St. <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> accommodated to the Gospel times. The Prophets spake suitably to them, unto whom they preached; and the Apostle rightly understands by these expressions, the manifold and more clear Revelation of the will of God in Christ.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="18">18 And on my servants, and on my handmaid<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ens <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">To shew what all ought to be, that hope for to re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ceive any benefit or comfort from the promises of God, either in the Law or Gospel, the Old or New Testament; <ns0:hi>viz.</ns0:hi> such as seek and serve God; but to the disobedient and unbelieving, there is not a comfortable word in all the Book of God. Some read without the Pronoun on <ns0:hi>ser<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vants and handmaids</ns0:hi>; to shew that God doth not despise men of the lowest rank and condition in the World, but that the promises of the Spirit is made unto them also.</ns0:note>, I will pour out in those days of my spirit, and they shall prophesie:</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="19">19 And I will shew wonders <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">As <ns0:hi>St. Peter</ns0:hi> had declared the promises unto such as would be drawn by the cords of Love: so here, on the o<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther side, he us<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>th threatnings, and declares the terrors of the Lord, if so that they will be perswaded. These wonders were such as did precede the Destruction of <ns0:hi>Ierusa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lem,</ns0:hi> or shall forerun the Destruction of the whole World.</ns0:note> in heaven above, and signs in the earth beneath; blood, and fire, and vapour of smoak.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="20">20 The sun shall be turned into darkness <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">This agrees with the other words in the fore-cited Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phecy, <ns0:hi>Ioel</ns0:hi> 2.31. How these amazing signs shall be ful<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />filled, whether literally, and by what means; Or whether onely, that the consternation and dread upon men shall be so great, as expecting the change of the whole frame of nature; is not so material for us to know, as it is to be always prepared for it.</ns0:note>, and the moon into blood, before that great and notable <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, Manifest and illustri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ous days; and it may be taken in a comfortable sense, and will be a comfortable day indeed, to all that prepared<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>y wait for it; for 'tis the day of the Lord, 'tis Christ's day, in which he will be magnified over his enemies, and in his friends, children, and servants.</ns0:note> day of the Lord come<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="21">21 And it shall come to pass, <ns0:hi>that</ns0:hi> 
                  <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Rom. 10.13.</ns0:note> whosoever shall call on the Name of the Lord <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">That he may prepare thus a people for the Lord; the Apostle shews by what means they and we may escape. Pray in faith unto him: The Name is that whereby any one is known; and the Lords Name is his Attributes, Good<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ness, Power, Wisdom, Faithfulness, <ns0:hi>&c. Prov.</ns0:hi> 18.10. <ns0:hi>The name of the Lord is a strong tower: the righteous runneth unto it, and is safe.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>, shall be saved.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="22">22 Ye men of Israel, hear these words; Jesus of Nazareth <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">For so <ns0:hi>Pilate</ns0:hi> had called our Saviour through con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tempt, in his Superscriptions on the Cross, and that they might certainly know of whom he spake, and that he was not now (as formerly) ashamed to own him: he men<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tions our Saviour under that name here,</ns0:note> a man approved <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">demonstrated, and beyond any contradiction, proved to be the Messiah: (for this was that great truth St. <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> Preached upon, that Christ whom <ns0:hi>Pilate</ns0:hi> had condemned, and called <ns0:hi>Iesus of Nazareth,</ns0:hi> was indeed the <ns0:hi>Son of God,</ns0:hi> and the true Mes<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />siah.)</ns0:note> of God among you, by miracles, wonders and signs <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">The critical difference is not so material; It was ordinary to add many words, to shew the greatness of the matter spoken of; indeed all sorts of wonderful works Christ did, and so many, and so great, as no variety of words can express.</ns0:note>, which God did by him in the midst of you, as ye your selves also know <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">Those that are not convinced, are self-condemned.</ns0:note>:</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="23">23 Him <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap 4.28.</ns0:note>, being delivered by the determinate counsel and the foreknowledged of God <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">That the Apostle might take away the offence of the Cross of Christ, he declares unto them, that he did not suf<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fer by chance, but by the wise and holy Providence of God, who had ordered, and by his Prophets foretold, what he should suffer before he did enter into glory, <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 24.26.                   </ns0:note>, <ns0:note n="‡" place="margin">Chap. 5 30.</ns0:note> ye have taken, and by wicked hands <ns0:note n="⸫" place="bottom">By the <ns0:hi>Romans</ns0:hi> who were truly <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, with<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />out any Law of God: What the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> urged or occasioned the <ns0:hi>Romans</ns0:hi> to do, is charged justly upon them as their Act.</ns0:note> have crucified <ns0:hi>g</ns0:hi> and slain:</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="24">24 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Ver. 32. Chap. 3.15. & 4.10 & 10.40. & 13.30, 34. & 17.31. Rom. 4.24. and 8.11. 1 Cor. 6.14. and 15.15. Gal. 1.1. 1 Thes. 1.10. Heb. 13.20.</ns0:note> Whom God hath raised up <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">Christ rose by his own Power <ns0:hi>as God</ns0:hi>; it being perhaps too strong meat to be given at first to such who were under so great prejudices against our Saviour: but by consequence in the following discourse, he sufficiently shews it.</ns0:note>, having loosed <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">The same word <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, variously pointed, signifying either a cord or pain, the metaphor of loosing agrees with it.</ns0:note> the pains of death <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">Tho our Lord endured now more pain, after he had said, <ns0:hi>It is fulfilled,</ns0:hi> and had yeilded up the Ghost: yet whilest he was in the grave, being under the power of death, the pains of death are said to be loosed at his Resurrection.</ns0:note>, because it was not possible that he should be holden of it <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">Long, much less for ever; being such an one as <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> spake of.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="25">25 For David speaketh <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 16.8. <ns0:hi>I foresaw the Lord always before my face.</ns0:hi> In the <ns0:hi>Psalm</ns0:hi> it is, <ns0:hi>I have set the Lord</ns0:hi>: the Apostle follow<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing the reading of the Seventy, then in use and known; and to the same sense; for by Faith we both see God, and place our confidence in him. <ns0:hi>David,</ns0:hi> and especially our Sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />viour, doing and enduring all things as in the sight of God, whom he knew to be both careful of him, and ready to help him. Thus in all troubles, there is no such approved comfort, as the seeing or acknowledging the Will of God conce<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ning them, his Power to preserve us under them, and his promises to deliver us from them. <ns0:hi>Christ</ns0:hi> and all that <ns0:hi>are Christs,</ns0:hi> do conflict under the eye, and in the sight of God; as Souldiers whilest their General looks on.</ns0:note> concerning him, I soresaw the Lord always before my face, for he is on my right hand <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">The place of the Advocate, for one that is accused or endangered.</ns0:note>, that I should not be moved.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="26">26 Therefore <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">Because of Gods nearness to, or presence with him.</ns0:note> did my heart rejoyce <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">Christs and his peoples joy is solid and true, real and in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ward, and may bear the rest, <ns0:hi>res severa est verum gaudium.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>, and my tongue <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">In the 16. <ns0:hi>Psalm, ver.</ns0:hi> 9. 'tis my glory, as the tongue is frequently called; communicating our thoughts or appre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />hensions by speech, being the excellency of a reasonable Creature.</ns0:note> was glad: moreover also, my flesh <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">Or my body:</ns0:note> shall rest <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">Or be in the grave, as in a Tabernacle, (ordinarily a moveable, always no durable a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />biding place)</ns0:note> in hope <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">That is of the Resurrection, and going out of that Tabernacle of the grave.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="27">27 Because thou wilt not leave my <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">That is <ns0:hi>me</ns0:hi>; the Soul is put for the person, as <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 13.1. <ns0:hi>Let every soul be subject:</ns0:hi> and sometimes for a dead Body, as <ns0:hi>Levit.</ns0:hi> 19.28. <ns0:hi>Numb.</ns0:hi> 5.2. and in divers other places, <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> that signifies a Soul, is so used.</ns0:note> soul in hell<ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">The word <ns0:gap reason="foreign">

                     </ns0:gap>, is put <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ither for the grave, or for the place of the damned. Being these words are alledg'd as a proof of Christs Resurrection, and that our Saviours Soul was cer<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tainly in Paradice, where he promised to the penitent thief, that he should be with him: it seems rather to be mean'd of the grave, which according to this Prophecy, could not hold our blessed Saviours body so long, as that it should corrupt in it. If <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> by <ns0:hi>his Soul,</ns0:hi> here did mean our Sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />viour, because he was as it were the Soul of his Soul, and Life of his Life, it shews how he did, and how we ought to value him.</ns0:note>, neither wilt thou suffer thine<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> holy One <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">As being Anointed, Sanctified, and sent by God.</ns0:note> to see corruption.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="28">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:374" />28 Thou hast made known to me <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">God is frequently said to make these mercies known to us, which he bestows upon us: (The ways of Life) of of a true Life; which is Life indeed. <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> in these words celebrates Gods delivering of him from his grievous afflicti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ons and exile: (in which he was looked upon by others, and by himself, as a dead man) yet was brought again to see the Temple, and enjoy the Ordinances of God; without which, his life was as no life unto him. So our Saviour, af<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ter his Death and Passion, arose, and Ascended into Hea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ven, and lives for ever to make Intercession for us.</ns0:note> the ways of life; thou shalt make me full of joy with thy coun<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tenance <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">That is, with thy presence<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> or manifestation of thy love and fa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vour.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="29">29 Men <ns0:hi>and</ns0:hi> brethren <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">St. <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> bespeaks this attention and favour; intima<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ting, he was one of the same Nation with themselves, than which nothing could more recommend him.</ns0:note>, <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                     <ns0:hi>Or,</ns0:hi> I may.</ns0:note> let me freely speak unto you of the <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Kin. 2.10. Chap. 13.36.</ns0:note> patriarch David <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> was had in great veneration, and his memory very precious a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mongst this people, as was <ns0:hi>Abrahams, Isaacs,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Iacobs</ns0:hi>; who were the chief of their Fathers:</ns0:note>, that he is both dead and buried <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">as in the 1 <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> 2.10. and else where is recorded of him, which they firmly be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lieved.</ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">Or Monument is with us; either not wholly spoiled by the <ns0:hi>Barbarous</ns0:hi> enemies, who had destroyed <ns0:hi>Ie<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rusalem</ns0:hi>; or rather repaired after the Captivity, to keep up the memory of so great and good a man. But by this it appeared, that <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> did not speak these things concern<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing himself, who must needs have seen corruption; (them<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />selves being witnesses) for on that account they respected his Tomb, as being the Repository of his ashes.</ns0:note>, and his sepulchre is with us unto this day:</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="30">30 Therefore being a prophet <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Rom. 1.3. 2 Tim. 2.8.</ns0:note>, and knowing that God had sworn with an oath <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">Not barely had sworn, which had been sufficient; but to shew the excellency of the matter, and the necessity of our believing of it, as also the solemnity of the words, <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 132.11.</ns0:note> to him, that of the fruit of his loyns <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">Such as should descend from him, as the Virgin <ns0:hi>Mary</ns0:hi> did.</ns0:note>, according to the flesh <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">As to his human Nature, which our Saviour did truly partake of, being in the form of a servant.</ns0:note>, he would raise up Christ, <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">By the Power of the Holy Ghost in the womb of his Virgin-mother as to his <ns0:hi>Incarnation</ns0:hi>; and by the same Power out of the grave, in his Resurrection.</ns0:note> to sit on his thro<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">

               <ns0:p n="42">42 And they continued stedfastly <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">Speak the reality of their Conversion, and that they were not onely for the present affected with what they had heard and seen.</ns0:note> in the apo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stles doctrine and fellowship, and in <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Ver. 46.</ns0:note> breaking of bread, and in prayers <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">These three parts of worship were fre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />quently, if not always in those purer times used together: tho some understand by breaking of bread, their civil fel<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lowship and community; yet <ns0:hi>breaking</ns0:hi> being a holy rite used by our Saviour, at the institution of his Supper, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 26 26. and breaking of bread being here put in conjuncti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on with Preaching and Praying, the celebration of the Eucharist, if not onely mean d, is chiefly to be understood in this place. <ns0:hi>(Prayers)</ns0:hi> all those kind of Prayers mentioned by St. <ns0:hi>Paul.</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Tim.</ns0:hi> 2.1. as also their <ns0:hi>frequent</ns0:hi> praying, is implyed; thus by an united force, they laboured to pull down mercies upon themselves and others, and to do violence unto the Kingdom of Heaven.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
